history.summary: The hilltop temple complex on Tekri, the 300-ft conical hill at Dewas whose two principal shrines are Chhoti Mata (Chamunda Mata) and Badi Mata (Tulja Bhavani), with numerous other temples (Hanuman, Ram, Bhairav, Navdurga, Shiva and a Jain temple) spread over the hill and explored on foot. Legend calls Tekri a Rakt Peeth where drops of Mata Sati's blood fell; the self-manifested goddesses are believed to be sisters (Tulja Bhavani the elder). The town's name is believed to come from Devivasini/Dev-vas, the goddess's residence on the hill. The complex's age is disputed (9th century / 1100-1200 years / timeless); Swami Shivom Tirtha wrote its history in 'Sadhan Shikhar' and E. M. Forster in 'The Hill of Devi' (1953). name: Tekri Mandir
town_description: Dewas is a city in the Malwa region of Madhya Pradesh, about 34-35 km from Indore; its name is believed to derive from 'Dev-vas' (abode of the deity), referring to the goddess shrines on the Tekri hill. It was formerly a 15-gun salute princely state.

travel.road: Dewas lies on the Indore-Bhopal corridor; the hilltop is reached by a broad flight of stone steps, a sliding path, or a ropeway (two-way ropeway ticket reported around Rs 150)

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (winter); Navratri draws lakhs of pilgrims but expect heavy crowds
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM - 9:00 PM (verify: one listing shows 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM)
